summary: Taloyoak Airport (YYH) is a small regional airport serving the Inuit hamlet of Taloyoak on the Boothia Peninsula in Nunavut, Canada. Located well above the Arctic Circle on the shores of Spence Bay, it is one of the most northerly airports in mainland North America and serves as a critical lifeline for the remote community, which has no road access. The airport primarily supports scheduled passenger flights, charter operations, and medical evacuation services.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Taloyoak Airport?
A: The airport is served primarily by regional carriers operating flights from Iqaluit and other Nunavut communities, with connections typically routed through Yellowknife or other hub airports.

Q: Does Taloyoak Airport have terminal facilities?
A: As a small community airport, it has a modest terminal building suitable for the limited daily traffic, with basic amenities for passengers.

Q: Is there road access to Taloyoak?
A: No, the community is fly-in only with no road connections to other settlements. Travel is by air year-round or by seasonal sea-ice or open-water routes used locally.

Q: What is the best time to fly to Taloyoak?
A: Summer months (June through August) generally offer the most reliable weather conditions, though Arctic weather can cause delays at any time of year.
transport_tips: There are no roads connecting Taloyoak to other communities, so the airport is the primary means of access for visitors. All visitors should expect to arrange accommodations in advance, as the hamlet has very limited lodging options. Be prepared for potential weather-related flight delays, which are common in the Arctic, and consider building flexibility into travel plans.
local_tip: Pack warm clothing regardless of the season, as temperatures can drop unexpectedly even in summer, and the airport is an unheated walk between the terminal and aircraft in many cases.
